extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers (especially those attempting characters unlike themselves; 'dominant paradigm' writers, workshop participants, teachers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft guidance for creative writers on creating accurate, sensitive, and fully realized characters whose race, gender, sexual orientation, age, or species differ from the author's. Emphasizes exercises, nuts-and-bolts techniques, and workshop-derived practices to build skill and reduce anxiety about 'getting it wrong.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray difference with increased skill and sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to increase writers’ skill and sensitivity in portraying difference in their fiction (racial, ethnic, gender, sexual orientation, age, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book's stated aim is both to increase skill and sensitivity and to allay anxieties about 'getting it wrong.' It provides techniques, exercises, and examples developed from workshops to help achieve this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create richer and more accurate characters with 'differences'
rubrics_metrics.description: Use characterization methods that produce richer, more accurate portrayals of characters who differ from the author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual 'discusses basic aspects of characterization and offers elementary techniques, practical exercises, and examples' specifically intended to help writers make characters more accurate and fully realized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use practical, nuts-and-bolts techniques and workshop exercises
rubrics_metrics.description: Favor practical, concrete craft techniques and exercises over abstract admonitions when learning to write other characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Described as a 'nuts-and-bolts approach,' the book grew out of a workshop and includes exercises developed from that workshop to 'help flex writerly muscles' and teach usable methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge and manage anxiety about 'getting it wrong'
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize writers' fears about misrepresenting others but do not let fear prevent attempting to write outside one's experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors explicitly aim to 'allay' anxieties and 'encourage people to acknowledge their fears and concerns, but also to try anyway.' Exercises and practice are presented as ways to reduce this anxiety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of and avoid relying on stereotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand past and present stereotypes and avoid reproducing them in characterization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews and the book emphasize learning about 'past and present stereotypes' and present exercises to help writers step outside stereotypical thinking and create more nuanced portrayals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply methods across multiple axes of difference
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques are intended to be applicable not only to race/ethnicity but to gender, sexual orientation, age, and other significant differences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The origin anecdote expands from ethnic difference to 'gender, sexual orientation, and age' and the manual addresses these varied problems together; guidance and exercises are meant to transfer across axes of difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create fully realized, well-rounded characters substantially different from oneself
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim for characters who are 'fully realized' and 'well-rounded' even when they are 'substantially different from oneself.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book is recommended for producing characters 'substantially different from oneself' and is explicitly recommended as reading for 'dominant paradigm' writers to learn this skill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray complexity of human (and non-human) experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Depict the complexity and multifaceted nature of experience, including non-human experiences in genre fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers note the book helps 'develop characters to exhibit the complexity of the human experience (and, since we're talking genre here, multifaceted non-human experiences as well),' suggesting exercises and examples address both human and non-human characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step outside one's own ROAARS through deliberate practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Use exercises to 'step outside their own ROAARS' (the authors' phrasing for the writer's familiar range of assumptions/experience) to broaden perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book 'presents exercises to help writers step outside their own ROAARS,' developed from workshops; these exercises are presented as a concrete way to expand a writer's representational reach and sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted pedagogical use (workshops, schools, and classrooms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the material as classroom/workshop-ready instruction for teaching writers how to handle difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews recommend the book for 'schools, colleges, and creativity workshops, and sociology classes,' indicating the content is organized and practical enough for pedagogical adoption and structured exercises.
